subject: humanities
passage: John Cage's 4′33″ (1952) instructs its performers to make no intentional sound for the work's duration of four minutes and thirty-three seconds, and audiences have sometimes received it as a provocation or a joke. Cage had come to believe that true silence does not exist, a conviction strengthened by a visit to a soundproof chamber in which he still heard sounds that he attributed to his own body. He therefore rejected the idea that the piece consists of silence. ______ he intended the work to turn listeners' attention to the sounds that are always present, such as rustling programs, distant traffic, and the breathing of the audience, and to invite them to hear those sounds as music.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

explanation.why: The third sentence says Cage rejected one description of the piece: that it consists of silence. The last sentence gives the description he accepted in its place: the piece directs attention to ever-present sounds. The transition must introduce a correction that replaces a rejected idea.
explanation.A: Incorrect. What Cage intended is not an example of his rejecting the idea of silence; it is the view he held instead.
explanation.B: Correct. "Rather" signals that the last sentence states what the piece is in place of what Cage said it is not.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" would mean Cage intended the work to highlight ambient sound in spite of rejecting the idea of silence, but that rejection is exactly why he saw the piece this way. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Similarly" introduces a parallel idea, but the last sentence states Cage's alternative view rather than a view like the one he rejected.
